condition: Strangulated femoral (Richter) hernia with small bowel obstruction
summary: 82-year-old woman with 2 days of colicky pain, vomiting and distension, no previous abdominal surgery; a small tender lump below the right inguinal ligament is found only on careful examination. Must-not-miss cause of SBO in a "virgin" abdomen; emergency surgery.

inputs.hpi: Two days of colicky central abdominal pain and vomiting, now brown-green. Abdomen bloated, last flatus yesterday. Never had abdominal surgery. Has not noticed any lump.

exam.general: Dry mucous membranes. Pulse 104, BP 108/64, temperature 37.6°C.
exam.abdomen: Distended, tympanic, tinkling bowel sounds, mild diffuse tenderness, no peritonism. No scars. Small (1.5 cm) tender, irreducible lump below the right inguinal ligament, lateral to the pubic tubercle. Rectum empty.

imaging.name: Abdominal X-ray
imaging.result: Multiple dilated small-bowel loops centrally; no gas in the colon.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Strangulated right femoral hernia (probable Richter type) with small bowel obstruction
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Strangulated right femoral hernia (probable Richter's) causing small bowel obstruction in a virgin abdomen. Resuscitate, NG decompression, CT if it will not delay theatre, emergency repair with bowel inspection.

mustNotMiss.note: SBO without previous surgery: an external hernia (femoral in elderly women) must be on the differential.
mustNotMiss.knownGapNote: PANE top 3 = cholecystitis, appendicitis, bowel obstruction (from the abdominal-pain template). No hernia: groin findings are only in exam text/chips, which PANE does not read. PANE: unlisted features count at DEFAULT_SENSITIVITY 0.30 for every disease and there is no false-positive term, so high-prior abdominal diseases (cholecystitis 0.15, GORD 0.12, PUD 0.10; male inguinal hernia x5) outrank the organ-specific disease after a single non-abdominal feature.
mustNotMiss.proposedFix: Feed exam chips ("Hernia present") and exam text into PANE features; in SBO with no previous surgery, surface external hernias (femoral/obturator) as must-not-miss.

mustInclude.note: CT defines the cause and ischaemia, provided it does not delay surgery in obvious strangulation.

mustExclude.note: A trial of non-operative (adhesional-SBO) management is wrong for a strangulated hernia.

guideline.name: WSES guidelines — emergency repair of complicated abdominal wall hernias (2017 update)
guideline.section: Diagnosis of strangulation (clinical signs, lactate, CPK, D-dimer, CT); timing of surgery; manual reduction only without strangulation; mesh in clean (CDC I) and clean-contaminated fields
guideline.citation: Birindelli A, Sartelli M, Di Saverio S, et al. 2017 update of the WSES guidelines for emergency repair of complicated abdominal wall hernias. World J Emerg Surg. 2017;12:37.

guideline.name: Bologna guidelines — adhesive small bowel obstruction (WSES 2017 update)
guideline.section: CT in suspected SBO; SBO in a patient without previous abdominal surgery (non-adhesive cause, e.g. hernia) needs a cause-specific diagnosis; signs of strangulation → surgery
guideline.citation: ten Broek RPG, Krielen P, Di Saverio S, et al. Bologna guidelines for diagnosis and management of adhesive small bowel obstruction (ASBO): 2017 update of the evidence-based guidelines from the World Society of Emergency Surgery ASBO working group. World J Emerg Surg. 2018;13:24.

guideline.name: HerniaSurge — International guidelines for groin hernia management
guideline.section: Diagnosis (clinical examination, ultrasound for uncertain swellings); watchful waiting in minimally symptomatic men; mesh repair (Lichtenstein, TEP/TAPP); groin hernia in women; femoral hernia; emergency repair
guideline.citation: HerniaSurge Group. International guidelines for groin hernia management. Hernia. 2018;22:1–165.

rationale: Permutation: dangerous presentation. The hernia is small and not the complaint; the CC is "vomiting and colicky abdominal pain". Tests that the obstruction is not treated as adhesional (no previous surgery) and that the plan is emergency surgery.
